The cap is expressly mutual and set at the greater of 12 months' Fees "paid or payable" and USD 1,000,000 (§21.1); "Fees" (§1.5) is a substantive base covering subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the cap is not illusory. §21.2 is a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and helpfully confirms data-restoration, replacement-service, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages. §21.3 places outside the cap breaches of confidentiality, data-protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP, and confirms Customer's payment of undisputed Fees is not "damages" subject to the cap. §21.4 preserves liability that cannot lawfully be limited, and §18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. No one-sided or hidden liability limitation appears elsewhere in the document. No redline needed.

Customer shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Vendor from and against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of content or materials provided by Customer for use in the Services (other than to the extent the claim is covered by Section 20.1) or Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

The indemnified party shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of the claim (delay excuses the indemnifying party only to the extent it is materially prejudiced), allow the indemnifying party to control the defence with counsel of its choice, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense. The indemnified party may participate with its own counsel at its own cost. The indemnifying party shall not settle a claim in a way that imposes liability, an admission, or a non-monetary obligation on the indemnified party without its prior written consent.

If the Services or Deliverables are, or in Vendor's reasonable opinion are likely to become, the subject of an infringement claim, Vendor shall at its expense and Customer's option procure the right for Customer to continue using them, or modify or replace them with functionally equivalent, non-infringing items that meet the requirements of this Agreement. quote: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
rationale: Section 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of every Deliverable (defined in 1.4 to include "other work product ... created specifically for Customer") in Vendor and leaves Customer only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence. That fails the preferred position (Customer owns deliverables and work product, with Vendor assignment) and also fails the fallback, which requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use and modify Deliverables. The other preferred limbs are already in the deal: 14.3 retains Vendor Technology for Vendor, 13.2 grants a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable, 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data, and 14.4 bars joint ownership. The redline therefore makes only the directional changes needed: Customer owns each Deliverable, Vendor assigns it, and the revocable term-limited licence now runs to Vendor so it cannot undercut Customer's ownership.
